Fleet and equipment maintenance in Victoria

Plan maintenance for trucks, heavy equipment and agricultural machinery around service records and operational requirements. Discuss the work and priorities directly with Clive Sampson.

Call Clive · 0474 372 852

Scheduled fleet and equipment maintenance

Preventive maintenance planning starts with the service schedule, operating conditions and records for each truck or machine. Share the work already due, developing faults and the next suitable maintenance window. Makes, models, kilometres and engine hours help frame the discussion.

For a mixed fleet, identify which equipment can be released first and which vehicles are needed for upcoming work. Clive will confirm the proposed scope, availability and scheduling arrangements for your fleet or equipment.

Information for maintenance planning

  • A vehicle and equipment list with identifying details.
  • Available service records, kilometres and engine hours.
  • Known faults or recurring concerns for each vehicle or machine.
  • Location, site access and when equipment can be made available.
  • Who can approve work and receive job updates.

Managing equipment from interstate

If you manage trucks or machinery in Victoria from another state, nominate the contact person at each Victorian location. Provide access details, service priorities and the person authorised to approve work. Agree scheduling and updates directly with Clive before a booking is confirmed.

Planned servicing and developing faults

Scheduled maintenance and an unexpected fault may need different arrangements. Identify equipment that has stopped working or needs assessment before its next scheduled use.

See truck servicing, heavy equipment servicing and agricultural machinery servicing for the relevant maintenance enquiry.

Agree the arrangements directly

Speak with Clive about the scope, location, timing and applicable charges before a booking is confirmed. Travel and access arrangements depend on the actual Victorian location and work required.

For a vehicle or machine requiring attention on site, discuss mobile field service.
